speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me determine the cause, have you noticed any specific triggers, such as eating certain foods, exertion, or stress?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet's Tooth (Denture Fracture/Choking on Denture) or Foreign Body Aspiration. Given the history of retching followed by choking and coughing, there is a high suspicion of an aspirated object or a fractured dental prosthesis causing airway obstruction and chest pain. I need to see the oral cavity and chest immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, Dental_Panoramic
